records.bodyText:
WHEN an official from the UK’s grid operator appeared at Holyrood’s energy committee last week, he quietly revealed that Scotland may have more AI data centres on the books than previously understood.
Martyn Day, the SNP MSP for Linlithgow, had put it to Matt Magill, a director at the National Energy System Operator (NESO), that there were “around 20 AI data centres in the pipeline”. Magill corrected him.
“There are closer to 30 in Scotland at the moment,” he said. “It is about 9.7 gigawatts (GW).”
This sparked a question: where and what are these extra potential data centres?
Around two dozen projects have so far been identified through planning documents and public announcements by Action to Protect Rural Scotland, with analysis by the countryside charity putting the potential electricity demand of the known projects at around 7.3GW.
THENATIONAL.SCOT Inside Scotland’s hidden pipeline of ‘phantom’ hyperscale data centres

With promises of creating thousands of employment opportunities and finally giving the public a stake in green power, a row over jobs numbers risks GB Energy being used as a tool to criticise the UK Labour government. But with the organisation’s Aberdeen headquarters officially opening this week, questions have been raised over what the body can achieve for Scotland’s net zero and renewables future.
GB Energy’s base is located at the Marischal Square development, which sparked a public backlash when it was constructed. Sitting above a branch of Costa coffee and overlooking the closed Illicit Still pub, the flagship headquarters does not even have a sign visible to the public. You wouldn’t know it was there.

records.title: Environmentalists Against Wind Turbines
records.bodyText:
Vineyard Wind: 800 MW doesn’t mean 800 MW 24/7.
Vineyard Wind is often described as an 800 MW project capable of powering around 400,000 homes. But there is an important distinction between nameplate capacity and actual electricity production.
Wind turbines only generate electricity when wind conditions allow, and output can also be affected by maintenance and other operating factors. So an 800 MW nameplate capacity does not mean 800 MW is continuously available around the clock.
The real question is: how much electricity will the project actually deliver over an entire year, and how does that compare with the “400,000 homes” figure? 
Are capacity figures sometimes misunderstood as actual, continuous power production?
#VineyardWind #WindPower #RenewableEnergy #EnergyDebate

records.title: Environmentalists Against Wind Turbines
records.bodyText:
BLOCK ISLAND WIND TURBINES HALF-MILE SPACING
SEPTEMBER 26, 2026
https://www.windtaskforce.org/.../block-island-wind...
The commercial fishing vessel F/V Mistress sank in rough weather near Block Island, Rhode Island, shortly after midnight on January 1, 2019, resulting in the tragic deaths of two crew members.
In a "targeted" dive, seven years after it sank, a shipwreck believed to be the commercial fishing vessel F/V Mistress was discovered in September 2026, resting just 50 feet from the base of turbine No. 1 at the Block Island Wind Farm.
Coast Guard records confirm that an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter abandoned its aerial search for the commercial fishing vessel F/V Mistress on January 1, 2019, due to the proximity to the Block Island wind turbines. The MH-60 is fully instrument-rated, leveraging a digital glass cockpit with advanced GPS (RNAV), TACAN, and Instrument Landing Systems (ILS) to navigate safely through dense clouds and zero-visibility conditions.
The community and local maritime groups had long-standing radar concerns that 500-foot commercial wind turbines—spaced just a half-mile apart—create clutter and "ghost readings" that severely hinder search and rescue (SAR) electronics during heavy storms.
The approval and environmental assessment of the Block Island Wind Farm—including the layouts, navigation pathways, and the specific 1/2 mile spacing between turbines—involved a collaborative review by federal and state agencies
The primary regulatory bodies responsible for reviewing and approving the project layouts and spacing were:
Federal Agencies:
U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE): environment
US Coast Guard: safety, radar, vessel transit zones
Bureau of Ocean Energy Management BOEM ): transmission right-of-way
National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA): adverse impacts, spacing turbines
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA): Aviation safety
Rhode Island State Agencies:
Rhode Island Coastal Resources Management Council (CRMC): lead permitting agency
Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management RIDEM: Local coast impacts
Note: # Long before construction of the Block Island wind project, on October 7, 2008, a meeting was held at the Hyannis Marina in Massachusetts regarding Cape Wind. The meeting involved the fishing industry addressing marine radar interference and the need for turbine spacing of two to three nautical miles. The Block Island turbines were in operation by 2016.
Offshore wind submarine cables can sell for up to $1000.00 per foot. Wind turbine advocates, politicians, and construction companies wanted the project to proceed with 1/2 mile spacing rather than two or more nautical miles.
#Follow the money

records.title: Scotland Against Spin
records.bodyText:
The UK government has paid almost twice as much to turn off windfarms in Scotland as it plans to spend on developing small modular nuclear reactors by the end of this decade, industry leaders have said.
The Nuclear Industry Association said ministers plan to invest £2.8 billion in the technology, compared with£5.1bn in so called constraint payments that have been made since 2021.
Some £1.04bn was forked out in constraint payments this year up until the end of August. This is up from £648 min the same period last year.
The UK Government wants to open small modular reactors in Scotland, potentially at former nuclear sites such as Torness, Hunterston, and Dounreay. All of these sites already have grid transmission connections. But this has been blocked by the Scottish government which holds planning powers.
SCOTSMAN.COM 'UK spends twice as much switching off windfarms as it does on nuclear reactors'

records.title: Scotland Against Spin
records.bodyText:
Herald letters
UKRAINE fired more than 1,000 drones at Russia, and Russia retaliated using drones to attack Ukraine's southern city of Zaporizhzhia.
This made me think about the greenhouse gases created by wars all around the world. Why have politicians and those of a green disposition never told us the volume of emissions created by the Russian war against Ukraine, and the emissions that will be created in rebuilding the shattered infrastructure?
Then, of course, there is mother nature, with her volcanoes, earthquakes, tsunamis, hurricanes and more. All emitting greenhouse gases which puny mankind can never control. No figure has been put on that either. What about music and sporting events? Do politicians really believe people will believe that buying an EV and a heat pump, and cycling to work and eating less meat, will save the planet?
Meanwhile, most of the rest of the world is still harvesting and using fossil fuels to drive their economies.
Clark Cross, Linlithgow.
